title: Resveratrol inhibits Toxoplasma gondii-induced lung injury, inflammatory cascade and evidences of its mechanism of action.
authors: Lu, Yu Nan; Shen, Xin Yu; Lu, Jing Mei; Jin, Guang Nan; Lan, Hui Wen; Xu, Xiang; Piao, Lian Xun
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究白藜芦醇抑制弓形虫感染引起的肺损伤及炎症机制，涉及分子对接但核心是药物抗炎与感染病理，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Toxoplasma gondii is an opportunistic protozoan that can infect host to cause toxoplasmosis. We have previously reported that resveratrol (RSV) has protective effects against liver damage in T. gondii infected mice. However, the effect of RSV on lung injury caused by T. gondii infection and its mechanism of action remain unclear. PURPOSE: In this work, we studied the protective effects of RSV on lung injury caused by T. gondii infection and explored the underlying mechanism. METHODS: Molecular docking and localized surface plasmon resonance assay were used to detect the molecular interactions between RSV and target proteins. In vitro, the anti-T. gondii effects and potential anti-inflammatory mechanisms of RSV were investigated by quantitative competitive-PCR, RT-PCR, ELISA, Western blotting and immunofluorescence using RAW 264.7 cells infected with tachyzoites of T. gondii RH strain. In vivo, the effects of RSV on lung injury caused by T. gondii infection were assessed by observing pathological changes and the expression of inflammatory factors of lung. RESULTS: RSV inhibited T. gondii loads and T. gondii-derived heat shock protein 70 (T.g.HSP70) expression in RAW 264.7 cells and lung tissues. Moreover, RSV interacts with T.g.HSP70 and toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), respectively, and interferes with the interaction between T.g.HSP70 and TLR4. It also inhibited the overproduction of inducible nitric oxide synthase, TNF-alpha and high mobility group protein 1 (HMGB1) by down-regulating TLR4/nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kappaB) signaling pathway, which is consistent with the effect of TLR4 inhibitor CLI-095. In vivo, RSV improved the pathological lung damage produced by T. gondii infection, as well as decreased the number of inflammatory cells in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and the release of HMGB1 and TNF-alpha. CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that RSV can inhibit the proliferation of T. gondii and T.g.HSP70 expression both in vitro and in vivo. RSV can inhibit excessive inflammatory response by intervening T.g.HSP70 and HMGB1 mediated TLR4/NF-kappaB signaling pathway activation, thereby ameliorating lung injury caused by T. gondii infection. The present study provides new data that may be useful for the development of RSV as a new agent for the treatment of lung damage caused by T. gondii infection.
abstract_zh: 背景：弓形虫（Toxoplasma gondii）是一种机会性原虫，可感染宿主引起弓形虫病。我们此前已报道白藜芦醇（RSV）对感染弓形虫的小鼠肝损伤具有保护作用。然而，RSV对弓形虫感染所致肺损伤的影响及其作用机制尚不清楚。目的：本研究探讨RSV对弓形虫感染所致肺损伤的保护作用，并探索其潜在机制。方法：采用分子对接和局域表面等离子体共振实验检测RSV与靶蛋白之间的分子相互作用。体外实验中，使用感染弓形虫RH株速殖子的RAW 264.7细胞，通过定量竞争PCR、RT-PCR、ELISA、Western blotting和免疫荧光技术研究RSV的抗弓形虫效应及潜在抗炎机制。体内实验中，通过观察肺组织病理变化和炎症因子表达，评估RSV对弓形虫感染所致肺损伤的影响。结果：RSV抑制了RAW 264.7细胞和肺组织中弓形虫载量及弓形虫来源的热休克蛋白70（T.g.HSP70）表达。此外，RSV分别与T.g.HSP70和Toll样受体4（TLR4）相互作用，并干扰T.g.HSP70与TLR4之间的结合。RSV还通过下调TLR4/核因子κB（NF-kappaB）信号通路，抑制诱导型一氧化氮合酶、TNF-α和高迁移率族蛋白1（HMGB1）的过度产生，这与TLR4抑制剂CLI-095的作用一致。体内实验中，RSV改善了弓形虫感染引起的肺组织病理损伤，并减少了支气管肺泡灌洗液中炎症细胞数量及HMGB1和TNF-α的释放。结论：这些发现表明，RSV在体外和体内均能抑制弓形虫增殖及T.g.HSP70表达。RSV可通过干预T.g.HSP70和HMGB1介导的TLR4/NF-kappaB信号通路激活，抑制过度炎症反应，从而改善弓形虫感染引起的肺损伤。本研究为RSV作为治疗弓形虫感染所致肺损伤的新型药物提供了新的数据支持。
